core_obligations: Retain the author inexact deformation and matching-sphere disjunction construction.
Build compact torus fibrations with flux and disjoint critical loci.
Use the fibre product and irrational translations to obtain infinitely many disjoint Lagrangian spheres.
difficulty_reason: The construction combines symplectic torus fibrations with irrational flux, fibre sums with rational elliptic surfaces, and a fibre product with separated singular loci. The resulting compact Morse-Bott-Lefschetz fibration has matching spheres whose intersections in the base are separated by accumulated irrational flux in the fibre. The preceding inexact-conifold construction is retained in full as the source-local model, rather than counted separately.

dedup.scope: Source absent from common baseline by DOI and arXiv2601.20438. Distinct from CP13-AG010/011/012 monodromy splitting theorems: this is a compact symplectic existence construction, not an algebraic splitting claim. The noncompact inexact-conifold corollary is supporting construction and is not counted separately.

compared.difference: Compact existence of infinitely many disjoint Lagrangian spheres versus pure braid monodromy retraction of an exact noncompact plumbing.
